nodes.source_anchor: paper A1.Thmtheorem1 uniform ζ; A1.SS1.p2.1 σ; A1.E12
nodes.attributed_restatement: Expectations of functions of U are the integrals of the corresponding first-coordinate functions against normalized surface measure.
Throughout HFT, n is a positive integer greater than1; Ω is open and nonempty in R^n. Thus the cited ball theorems include n=2.

A harmonic function is C² with zero Laplacian on an open set. Harmonicity on a non-open set E means extension to an open neighborhood of E. Functions are complex valued by default; the two tests here are real valued.
B is the open unit ball, B̄ its closure, S its boundary. σ is normalized surface area, σ(S)=1, equivalently the unique rotation-invariant Borel probability measure on S.
For a function harmonic on the closed ball (in the neighborhood-extension convention), its value at the center equals its normalized boundary average.
